entries.title: Criminal breach of trust
entries.summary: Requires entrustment or dominion over property and dishonest misappropriation, conversion, use or disposal contrary to a legal direction or relevant contract, or wilfully allowing it. A contractual dispute alone does not establish these elements.
entries.source_note: Historical reference copy; selected physical-document provisions only. Not a versioned consolidation of every amendment.

entries.title: Cheating
entries.summary: Defines cheating through deception and specified inducement, including delivery or retention of property, or an induced act or omission causing or likely to cause harm. Dishonest concealment can be deception. A later failure to perform a promise does not by itself show dishonest intention at the outset.
entries.source_note: Historical reference copy; selected physical-document provisions only. Not a versioned consolidation of every amendment.

entries.title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
entries.summary: Concerns cheating that dishonestly induces delivery of property or the making, alteration or destruction of a valuable security or something capable of becoming one. The deception and dishonest inducement must be established; a missing payment or disputed sale alone is insufficient.
entries.source_note: Historical reference copy; selected physical-document provisions only. Not a versioned consolidation of every amendment.

entries.title: False consideration in a transfer deed
entries.summary: Addresses dishonest or fraudulent participation in a deed transferring or charging property that contains a false statement about consideration or the intended beneficiary. A blank field, OCR error or valuation disagreement alone does not establish the required conduct and intent.
entries.source_note: Historical reference copy; selected physical-document provisions only. Not a versioned consolidation of every amendment.

entries.title: Criminal trespass
entries.summary: Requires entry onto property in another person’s possession with intent to commit an offence or to intimidate, insult or annoy, or unlawfully remaining after lawful entry with the specified intent. A boundary or ownership dispute alone is not proof of criminal trespass.
entries.source_note: Historical reference copy; selected physical-document provisions only. Not a versioned consolidation of every amendment.

entries.title: Forgery
entries.summary: Addresses making a false document with specified intent, including causing injury, supporting a claim or title, inducing a transfer or contract, or committing fraud. Whether a document is false must be examined under the relevant definition; an allegation in an uploaded paper is not proof.
entries.source_note: Historical reference copy; selected physical-document provisions only. Not a versioned consolidation of every amendment.

entries.title: Making a false document
entries.summary: Covers specified dishonest or fraudulent acts involving false authorship or authority, material alteration without lawful authority, and causing execution by a person unable to understand the document in the stated circumstances. A false statement in a document does not automatically satisfy this definition.
entries.source_note: Historical reference copy; selected physical-document provisions only. Not a versioned consolidation of every amendment.

entries.title: Forgery of valuable security, will, etc.
entries.summary: Concerns forgery of specified instruments, including valuable securities, wills, authorities and receipts. The instrument must fall within the statutory categories and the elements of forgery must be met; not every disputed property paper automatically qualifies.
entries.source_note: Historical reference copy; selected physical-document provisions only. Not a versioned consolidation of every amendment.

entries.title: Forgery for the purpose of cheating
entries.summary: Concerns forgery committed with the intention that the forged document be used for cheating. It requires both forgery and the specified intended use, rather than merely a document discrepancy.
entries.source_note: Historical reference copy; selected physical-document provisions only. Not a versioned consolidation of every amendment.

entries.title: Using a forged document as genuine
entries.summary: Concerns fraudulent or dishonest use of a forged document as genuine while knowing, or having reason to believe, that it is forged. Possessing or receiving a questioned document alone does not establish every element.
entries.source_note: Historical reference copy; selected physical-document provisions only. Not a versioned consolidation of every amendment.

entries.title: Criminal breach of trust
entries.summary: Subsection (1) defines criminal breach of trust through entrustment or dominion over property and specified dishonest handling or wilfully allowing it. Later subsections address punishment and particular roles. A mere unpaid debt or contract dispute does not automatically establish entrustment and dishonest misappropriation.
entries.source_note: NCRB reference text. Read the official text and applicable amendments before relying on it.

entries.title: Cheating
entries.summary: Subsection (1) defines cheating through deception and specified inducement or harm. Its illustrations distinguish dishonest intention at the time of inducement from a later breach of a promise initially made honestly. Subsection (4) addresses dishonest inducement to deliver property or deal with valuable securities.
entries.source_note: NCRB reference text. Read the official text and applicable amendments before relying on it.

entries.title: Cheating inducing delivery of property
entries.summary: Addresses cheating that dishonestly induces delivery of property, or making, altering or destroying a valuable security or something signed or sealed capable of becoming one. Verify the required deception and inducement; a property transfer itself is not evidence of cheating.
entries.source_note: NCRB reference text. Read the official text and applicable amendments before relying on it.

entries.title: False consideration in a transfer deed
entries.summary: Addresses dishonest or fraudulent execution of, or participation in, a property transfer or charge instrument containing a false statement about consideration or the intended beneficiary. Its wording and punishment must be checked independently of the historical IPC provision.
entries.source_note: NCRB reference text. Read the official text and applicable amendments before relying on it.

entries.title: Criminal trespass and house-trespass
entries.summary: Subsection (1) defines criminal trespass by reference to possession, entry or unlawfully remaining, and specified intent. Subsection (2) concerns house-trespass; subsections (3) and (4) provide punishment. An ownership disagreement or unauthorised entry alone is not a complete criminal finding.
entries.source_note: NCRB reference text. Read the official text and applicable amendments before relying on it.

entries.title: Making a false document
entries.summary: Defines specified dishonest or fraudulent acts involving false authorship or authority, unauthorised material alteration, or causing execution in the stated incapacity or deception circumstances. Covers documents and electronic records. A disputed recital alone does not establish all elements.
entries.source_note: NCRB reference text. Read the official text and applicable amendments before relying on it.

entries.title: Forgery
entries.summary: Subsection (1) addresses making a false document or electronic record with specified intent, including supporting a claim or title or committing fraud. Other subsections cover punishment and purposes including cheating. The definition of a false document and the required intent must be checked.
entries.source_note: NCRB reference text. Read the official text and applicable amendments before relying on it.

entries.title: Forgery for the purpose of cheating
entries.summary: Addresses committing forgery with the intention that the forged document or electronic record be used for cheating. A mismatch detected by OCR or analysis does not establish forgery or the required intent.
entries.source_note: NCRB reference text. Read the official text and applicable amendments before relying on it.

entries.title: Forgery of valuable security, will, etc.
entries.summary: Concerns forgery of the specified types of instruments, including valuable securities, wills, authorities and receipts. Both forgery and the statutory instrument category need to be established; the title of a property document is not sufficient by itself.
entries.source_note: NCRB reference text. Read the official text and applicable amendments before relying on it.

entries.title: Forged records and using them as genuine
entries.summary: Subsection (1) describes a forged document or electronic record. Subsection (2) addresses fraudulent or dishonest use as genuine while knowing or having reason to believe the record is forged. The source document alone cannot establish authenticity or a person’s knowledge.
entries.source_note: NCRB reference text. Read the official text and applicable amendments before relying on it.

entries.title: Repeal and savings
entries.summary: Repeals the IPC while preserving specified prior operations, liabilities, penalties, investigations, proceedings and remedies. The date and nature of the alleged conduct matter; the date of uploading or signing a document alone must not determine which criminal law governs.
entries.source_note: NCRB reference text. Read the official text and applicable amendments before relying on it.

entries.title: Sale and contract for sale
entries.summary: Defines sale as a transfer of ownership for a price paid, promised or partly paid and promised. Requires a registered instrument for tangible immovable property valued at ₹100 or more and for reversions or other intangible things. A contract for sale does not by itself create an interest in or charge on the property.
entries.source_note: Central provisions only; local amendments, exemptions and special property laws are outside this collection.

entries.title: Rights and liabilities of buyer and seller
entries.summary: Sets default rights and obligations, in the absence of a contract to the contrary, including specified disclosure of material defects in property or title, production of title documents, answering relevant questions, payment and delivery duties. Which duty applies depends on the facts and the contract.
entries.source_note: Central provisions only; local amendments, exemptions and special property laws are outside this collection.

entries.title: Mortgage definitions
entries.summary: Defines a mortgage as transfer of an interest in specific immovable property to secure specified debts or obligations, and describes mortgage types. The instrument’s substance matters; a loan or deposit of papers must not be classified solely by its label.
entries.source_note: Central provisions only; local amendments, exemptions and special property laws are outside this collection.

entries.title: Form of a mortgage
entries.summary: For principal money of ₹100 or more, a mortgage other than a mortgage by deposit of title deeds requires a registered instrument signed by the mortgagor and attested by at least two witnesses. Other cases and exceptions require reading the full section.
entries.source_note: Central provisions only; local amendments, exemptions and special property laws are outside this collection.

entries.title: Lease defined
entries.summary: Defines a lease of immovable property as a transfer of a right to enjoy it for a specified or implied time, or in perpetuity, for the stated consideration. Defines lessor, lessee, premium and rent. It does not turn every permission to occupy into a lease automatically.
entries.source_note: Central provisions only; local amendments, exemptions and special property laws are outside this collection.

entries.title: How leases are made
entries.summary: A lease from year to year, for a term exceeding one year, or reserving yearly rent requires a registered instrument under this section. It also addresses other leases and execution by lessor and lessee, subject to the stated proviso. Local tenancy laws and amendments are not covered here.
entries.source_note: Central provisions only; local amendments, exemptions and special property laws are outside this collection.

entries.title: Gift defined
entries.summary: Defines a gift as a voluntary transfer of certain existing property without consideration, accepted by or on behalf of the donee. Acceptance must occur during the donor’s lifetime and while the donor remains capable of giving; if the donee dies before acceptance, the gift is void.
entries.source_note: Central provisions only; local amendments, exemptions and special property laws are outside this collection.

entries.title: Form of a gift
entries.summary: For a gift of immovable property, specifies a registered instrument signed by or on behalf of the donor and attested by at least two witnesses. The Act’s savings, including those concerning gifts under Muhammadan law, must also be checked; this summary is not a universal rule for every gift.
entries.source_note: Central provisions only; local amendments, exemptions and special property laws are outside this collection.

entries.title: Compulsory registration
entries.summary: Lists instruments requiring registration, including gifts of immovable property, specified instruments affecting immovable-property rights of ₹100 or more, and certain leases. Subsection (1A) addresses contracts used for part performance; subsection (2) and the proviso contain exceptions. Not every agreement has identical registration requirements.
entries.source_note: Central section 17 only, PDF pages 1–3. State amendments and publisher comments in this hosted copy are excluded.

entries.title: Effect of non-registration
entries.summary: Limits the property effect and evidentiary use of documents required to be registered but left unregistered. The proviso allows specified use as evidence of a contract in a specific-performance suit or of a collateral transaction not requiring a registered instrument. Do not treat every unregistered paper as automatically void or unusable for every purpose.
entries.source_note: Central section 49 and its proviso only, PDF page 2. State amendment and publisher comments are excluded.

entries.title: What agreements are contracts
entries.summary: Requires free consent of competent parties, lawful consideration and object, and that the agreement not be expressly declared void. Preserves other laws requiring writing, witnesses or registration. Merely signing a paper does not establish all these conditions.
entries.source_note: Selected central provisions; summaries are not the full statute.

entries.title: Fraud in contractual consent
entries.summary: Defines specified acts committed with intent to deceive or induce entry into a contract, including knowing false assertions, active concealment and a promise made without intention to perform. Mere silence is generally not fraud unless there is a duty to speak or silence itself is equivalent to speech.
entries.source_note: Selected central provisions; summaries are not the full statute.

entries.title: Misrepresentation
entries.summary: Covers specified unwarranted positive assertions believed true, certain breaches of duty without intent to deceive, and causing a mistake about the substance of the agreement. Distinguish these consent issues from criminal offences rather than assuming they are the same.
entries.source_note: Selected central provisions; summaries are not the full statute.

entries.title: Voidability where consent is not free
entries.summary: Provides for voidability at the affected party’s option where consent was caused by coercion, fraud or misrepresentation, and describes an alternative remedy for fraud or misrepresentation. The ordinary-diligence exception for misrepresentation or fraudulent silence and the requirement that the conduct caused consent must be considered.
entries.source_note: Selected central provisions; summaries are not the full statute.
